title: 研究：将 parse_number() 实现为 SQLite 扩展：C 与 Rust 对比
author: Simon Willison
content:
8th November 2026

Research parse_number() as a SQLite extension: C vs Rust — Four SQLite extensions implement the same `parse_number()` behavior in C and Rust, with tests covering type preservation, parsing rules, and floating-point accuracy. The optimized C implementation was fastest at 16–19 ns per row, about twice as fast as the Rust versions and far faster than SQL `replace()`. Plain C was slower on decimals because it relied on `strtod()`, while a compact fast path closed that gap; all versions matched across 8 million fuzz checks.

I was out walking the dog when I got curious about how easy/difficult it would be to write a SQLite C extension that adds a parse_number() function for turning strings like -$1,234.56 or '12.5%' into numeric values that could be summed and sorted.

I fired up regular Claude chat (Opus 5.5) and prompted:

I'm thinking about a SQLite custom function 'parse_number(value)' that strips ',', '$', '£' and '%', handles a leading '-', and returns 'NULL' for anything it can’t parse

Explore the difference between building this as a SQLite extension in C v.s. in Rust - I want to compare performance and code complexity and size of the resulting.so(or whatever) file

This gave me a solid starting point - the Rust extension was 321 KB (using Rusqlite) and 298 KB (using sqlite-loadable-rs), while the C extension was 14 KB. But the Rust extension was faster!

Turns out that's because the Rust equivalent of C's strtod is "twice as fast". So I prompted:

Try writing your own C function for parsing text into a decimal number that catches up to or beats the Rust implementation

And it did:

Net cost per row over 2 million rows, lower is better:

first C new C rusqlite sqlite-loadable
Mixed data 67 ns 19 ns 46 ns 41 ns
Integers only 25 ns 16 ns 36 ns 32 ns
Decimals only 106 ns 18 ns 55 ns 47 ns

Finally, I had it rewrite the prototype as a research report to match the others in simonw/research by prompting this:

Clone simonw/research from GitHub and turn your above investigation into a research report as seen in that repository - you can give me a zip file to download that contains your new folder

Here's the resulting report.
aiSummary: 文章比较了用 C 和 Rust 实现的 SQLite parse_number() 扩展，发现经过手动优化的 C 版本速度更快，而 Rust 则更易开发且性能相近。
oneSentenceSummary: 文章比较了用 C 和 Rust 实现的 SQLite parse_number() 扩展，发现经过手动优化的 C 版本速度更快，而 Rust 则更易开发且性能相近。
summary: 作者研究了如何分别用 C 和 Rust 实现 SQLite 的 parse_number() 函数，将「-$1，234.56」或「12.5%」等格式化字符串转换为数值。作者先让 Claude Opus 5.5 生成初始实现，其中使用 rusqlite（321 KB）和 sqlite-loadable-rs（298 KB）的 Rust 版本速度都快于最初的 C 实现。不过，在提示 Claude 优化 C 版本后，得到的高效实现每行耗时仅为 16-19 ns，速度约为 Rust 的两倍。优化后的 C 扩展大小只有 14 KB。所有实现都通过了 8 million 次模糊测试，验证了正确性。最后，作者将这项研究整理成正式报告，发布在 simonw/research 仓库中。

mainPoints.point: 优化后的 C 实现在 parse_number() 扩展中胜过 Rust
mainPoints.explanation: 经过手动优化的 C 版本每行耗时 16-19 ns，约为 Rust 实现（36-46 ns）的一半，表明在这一特定解析任务中，精心优化的 C 代码可以胜过设计良好的 Rust 代码。

mainPoints.point: Rust 开发更容易，性能差距也比预期更小
mainPoints.explanation: 使用 rusqlite 和 sqlite-loadable-rs 的 Rust 实现速度快于最初的 C 代码，说明现代 Rust SQLite 扩展工具非常有效；此外，Rust 中与 C 的 strtod 对应的实现速度约为 C 的 strtod 的两倍。

mainPoints.point: 所有实现都通过了大规模模糊测试，验证了正确性
mainPoints.explanation: 8 million 次模糊测试检查验证了所有版本都能正确处理类型保留、解析规则和浮点精度，确保它们在多种输入情形下都可靠。

mainPoints.point: 文件大小差异凸显开发方式与部署之间的取舍
mainPoints.explanation: C 扩展编译后仅有 14 KB，而 Rust 版本为 298-321 KB，说明 C 能生成更精简的二进制文件，但需要投入更多手动优化工作。

keyQuotes: 我遛狗时突然好奇：编写一个 SQLite C 扩展有多容易或多困难？这个扩展可以添加 parse_number() 函数，把「-$1，234.56」或「12.5%」这样的字符串转换为可用于求和和排序的数值。
事实证明，这是因为 Rust 中与 C 的 strtod 对应的实现「速度快了两倍」。
